God chose us in Christ and adopted us as his children. How does knowing you are chosen and adopted affect you?
In Christ we have redemption and forgiveness according to the riches of his grace. What do these riches mean to you?
You were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit. What does the Spirit's seal assure you of?
Paul prays for the eyes of your heart to be enlightened. What would you like God to open your eyes to?
Paul says we were dead in our sins. Why is it important to remember where we came from?
"But God, being rich in mercy..." What does God's mercy mean to you today?
We are saved by grace through faith, and created for good works. What good works might God have prepared for you?
Christ has broken down the dividing wall of hostility. Where do you need Christ's peace between people?
The mystery is that the Gentiles are fellow heirs in Christ. Why is this such good news?
Paul calls himself the very least of all the saints. How does grace make us humble?
Paul prays you would know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge. How wide and deep is Christ's love to you?
God is able to do far more abundantly than all we ask or think. What would you ask him for?
Paul urges walking with humility, gentleness and patience. Which of these do you need most?
Christ gave gifts to build up the body until we grow up in him. How are you helping others grow?
Put off the old self and put on the new. What do you need to put off, and what to put on?
"Be kind to one another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, as God in Christ forgave you." Who needs this from you?
"Walk in love, as Christ loved us." What would walking in love look like today?
Paul says, "Walk as children of light." Where do you need God's light?
Paul says to make the best use of the time and be filled with the Spirit. How can you use your time wisely?
Paul compares marriage to Christ's love for the church. What does Christ's love for his church show you?
Paul speaks to children and parents. How can family relationships honour the Lord?
Paul says to work as serving the Lord, not people. How could this change how you approach your work?
Which piece of the armour of God do you most need today, and why?
Paul asked for prayer to speak boldly. Who could you pray for in this way?
